subject.title: tools.deny not enforced for claude-cli backend MCP — agents can call denied MCP tools

question: Which Claude CLI MCP enforcement model should OpenClaw own for `tools.deny`: pre-filter generated MCP config, map effective denies to Claude `--disallowedTools`, or fail closed for unsupported MCP deny patterns?
rationale: The issue is a real security-boundary bug, but the prior direct fix showed that choosing the wrong enforcement layer can widen access, so maintainer intent is needed before repair automation should proceed.

options.title: Owner-reviewed pre-handoff enforcement
options.body: Enforce the effective OpenClaw policy before Claude CLI sees MCP servers, with tests for exact MCP tools, wildcard entries, server-level denies, and deny-wins precedence.

options.title: Claude-side disallowedTools mapping
options.body: Translate effective OpenClaw deny entries into Claude CLI `--disallowedTools` where semantics match, and fail closed or diagnose entries that cannot be represented safely.

options.title: Document unsupported denies only
options.body: Leave runtime behavior unchanged and warn that Claude CLI MCP denial is not enforced, accepting the current security gap for compatibility.

recommendation.title: Owner-reviewed pre-handoff enforcement
recommendation.body: Enforce the effective OpenClaw policy before Claude CLI sees MCP servers, with tests for exact MCP tools, wildcard entries, server-level denies, and deny-wins precedence.

likelyOwner.reason: Most of the relevant Claude CLI MCP handoff and bundle config history points to this owner as the best available decision route.
